transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can’t keep my thoughts organized anymore, and it’s getting hard to make even simple decisions at work, which recently led to some scheduling mistakes with my clients. My supervisor suggested I talk to someone after I admitted my mind felt completely scattered, especially with the stress of balancing my job as a personal care aide with helping my sick mother.
Did these problems start after a specific stressful event, and have they been going on for less than 6 months or for 6 months or longer?

These big mood swings have actually been happening off and on for a couple of years, but they got a lot worse over the past year when my mom's diabetes complications escalated. This current phase where I feel so scattered and unable to think straight has been going on for about a month now.
During this past month, have you also been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or has it been more mainly worry and feeling overwhelmed?

Yes, it has definitely been a deep, empty feeling of being down, like a heavy gray cloud is sitting on my chest and making me tear up for no reason. I’ve also completely lost touch with things I used to enjoy, like car restoration and board-game nights, because I just feel too hollow and exhausted to care.
Over the past month, have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

Yes, my sleep is terrible because I either lie awake worrying about my mom or wake up panicked at 3 AM about work, leaving me so exhausted that I feel completely drained by noon. I also carry this constant, heavy guilt, feeling like a terrible son and husband who is failing everyone, though my appetite hasn't really changed much.
Before this past month, had you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day, even when there wasn’t a major stressor?

Yes, I've definitely had stretches like that over the last couple of years where I'd feel completely drained and hopeless for weeks at a time. Even before my mom's health got really bad, I would crash into those low moods off and on. The recent stress has made it much worse, but these down periods aren't entirely new to me.
Have you had at least one previous episode like this that lasted 2 weeks or longer and then fully or mostly improved before the current one?

Yes, absolutely. Over the last couple of years, those heavy, drained periods would last for several weeks and then mostly clear up or shift into a wired phase before this current stretch started. It definitely used to improve or change before I crashed into this latest month-long low.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, had racing thoughts, or did risky things like overspending or taking on too many projects?

Yes, I've had periods like that for a couple of years where I feel weirdly amped up for days, sleeping only three or four hours but waking up totally charged. During those times, I feel like I'm powered by a motor and am the only one who can handle everything, so I'll take on way too many projects at once like deep cleaning, remodeling, and extra work shifts.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, had racing thoughts, or did risky things like overspending or taking on too many projects?

Yes, those "high" periods usually last for a week or more, and I also get incredibly irritable and snap at my wife or people in traffic over tiny things. I feel so energized that I sleep only three or four hours, take on way too many clients, and truly believe I'm the only one who can fix everything. These intense swings have been happening off and on for about a couple of years now.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was so high or irritable and your energy so increased that it caused major problems, led to hospitalization, or made others say you seemed out of control?

I’ve never been hospitalized, but those wired and irritable phases have definitely caused major problems for me. I've had clients reassigned at work and a warning from my supervisor about losing hours, plus my wife had to take over managing our bills because I keep dropping the ball and snapping at her.
During your high-energy or low periods, have you ever had hallucinations, felt paranoid, or believed things that others said were not true?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I haven't had hallucinations, felt paranoid, or believed things that weren't true during either my high or low periods.
Have your high-energy periods ever become so severe that you were completely unable to function, needed hospitalization, or had to be stopped by others because you seemed out of control?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized or completely out of control, but those wired phases have definitely caused some serious disruptions. I end up sleeping very little, taking on way too much, and getting so irritable that my supervisor warned me I could lose hours, and my wife had to take over managing our bills.

During those high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or were the symptoms severe enough to cause marked problems in your work or relationships without needing hospitalization?

No, I've never been hospitalized, but those periods definitely caused major problems at work and at home. I made scheduling errors that got clients reassigned and earned me a warning from my supervisor, and my wife had to take over managing our bills because I was so irritable and kept dropping the ball.
In the past month, have your symptoms been severe enough to make it very hard to function at work or at home, or have they mainly been uncomfortable but still manageable?

Yes, it has been extremely hard to function at both work and home, far beyond just being uncomfortable. Because of my scheduling mistakes, I've had clients reassigned and received a warning from my supervisor about losing my hours. At home, my wife has had to take over managing the bills and reminders because I keep dropping the ball, and my mood swings have caused a lot of strain between us.
Have you ever, during your depressed or high-energy periods, heard or seen things other people couldn’t, or had very strong beliefs that others said were not true?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard or seen things that weren't there, and I don't hold any unusual beliefs that others would find untrue. My mind gets very scattered, but it has never gone that far.

Just to confirm, during your worst depressed or high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or strong false beliefs, like hearing voices or being convinced of something others said was not true?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices, seen things that aren't there, or held any strong false beliefs like that during either my high or low periods.
During this past month, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, thoughts of hurting yourself, or felt so slowed down that it is hard to get out of bed or do basic tasks?

I have caught myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up one day, or that everyone would be better off without me, though I haven't made any plans to hurt myself. Basic tasks have also become incredibly exhausting; even just showering, getting dressed, or driving to a client's house leaves me feeling completely wiped out by noon.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or making a plan to end your life, or have you been moving or speaking much more slowly than usual lately?

I do have thoughts that it wouldn't be so bad if I didn't wake up, or that everyone would be better off without me because of my mistakes, but I haven't made any plans to hurt myself. And while I feel incredibly exhausted and drained all the time now, I haven't noticed myself actually speaking or moving any slower.
Have you had any thoughts of actually hurting yourself, or made any plan or intent to end your life?

No, I don't have any plans or any intention of hurting myself. I just sometimes get those thoughts that it would be easier if I didn't wake up, or that my family would be better off without me screwing things up. But I have never made a plan or had any desire to actually act on it.
During this current low period, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or feeling so slowed down that others have commented on it?

No, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking any slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. I just feel incredibly exhausted and drained, but my physical movements and speech seem to be at their usual pace.
During this current low period, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or feeling so slowed down that others have commented on it?
Like I mentioned, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking any slower, and no one has commented on anything like that. I just feel incredibly tired and exhausted all the time.
Have you noticed feeling or moving much slower than usual, or has anyone else commented that your speech or movements seem slowed down during this depression?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that, and no one has commented that my speech or movements seem slower. I just feel extremely fatigued and completely exhausted all the time.
During this current depressed period, have you been moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or has anyone else commented that you seem slowed down?
No, I really haven't noticed myself moving or speaking any slower, and no one has commented on anything like that. I just feel extremely fatigued and completely drained of energy all the time.
Have you noticed feeling or moving much slower than usual, or has anyone else commented that your speech or movements seem slowed down during this depression?
I really haven't noticed moving or speaking any slower, and no one has said anything to me about it. I just feel extremely exhausted and tired.

No, I haven't noticed myself moving or speaking any slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. I just feel incredibly exhausted and tired all the time.
Have you noticed feeling or moving much slower than usual, or has anyone else commented that your speech or movements seem slowed down during this depression?
No, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slower, and no one has commented on it. I just feel incredibly exhausted and tired overall.
During this current depression, have you noticed feeling much slower in your thinking, speech, or movements, or has anyone else commented that you seem slowed down?

My thinking definitely feels incredibly slowed down and blank, like when I stare at the medication log at work and read the same line over and over without it registering, making decisions feel impossible. However, while my brain feels completely stalled, I haven't noticed my physical movements or speech slowing down, and no one has commented on that specifically.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual during this depression, or have other people commented that you seem slowed down?
No, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. Physically, I seem to be moving at my normal pace despite how exhausted I feel.
During this current depression, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or have other people commented that you seem slowed down?
No, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. I just feel incredibly tired, but my physical pace seems normal.
During this depression, have you noticed feeling much slower in your movements or speech, or have other people commented that you seem slowed down?
No, I haven't really noticed my physical movements or speech slowing down, and no one has commented on that. I just feel extremely fatigued and exhausted.
Have you noticed feeling or moving much slower than usual during this depression, or have other people commented that you seem slowed down?
No, I haven't really noticed myself moving slower physically, even though I feel extremely exhausted. My brain definitely feels slow to process things, but my actual movements seem normal.
